math_review: Both endpoint questions in the bilinear analytic annihilator of Hayman and Lingham, Problem 7.72, have negative answers under the printed negative-kernel convention. The norm-one input v(z)=z/bar(z) on the unit disc annihilates every integrable analytic test function, while its Beurling transform is 1+log|z|^2 and is essentially unbounded. Explicit polynomials v_m(z)=z^2 sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-|z|^2)^j lie in the same annihilator, have norm one and have transform norm H_m, the m-th harmonic number. Each fixed polynomial has bounded transform, but no common uniform constant exists.
priority_scope: This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of consequences of classical formulas, with a self-contained proof. Iwaniec published the exact nonpolynomial witness, output and primitive in 1986. Gill published the general positive-angular transform formula in 2010; the polynomial formula and harmonic-number norm follow by elementary specialization. The 2019 Hayman-Lingham book attributes resolution of Problem 7.72 to Volberg. Its cited reference 52 is the 2008 Banuelos-Janakiraman finite-p paper; the current audit did not locate an explicit full-target account there or a separate Volberg proof. This limitation does not refute the book attribution. No new solution, witness, transform mechanism, first polynomial construction, first harmonic-number calculation or current worldwide openness is claimed. Priority for an earlier explicit combined statement in the exact annihilator notation remains unestablished.
